newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE FLOTATION PUT BACK ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEWCASTLE FLOTATION PUT BACK ON TRACK.

text.p: English Premier League club Newcastle United were pressing ahead on Wednesday with plans for a stock market flotation following the appointment of Kenny Dalglish to succeed Kevin Keegan as manager.
Details of the timetable and structure of a listing expected to value the club at some 160 million pounds ($265 million) are expected in the next few days, possibly as early as Thursday.
The club would not comment on the timing of the announcement. Trading in the shares is likely to begin by April.
Former Liverpool and Blackburn Rovers manager Dalglish, appointed on Tuesday night, has plenty of support among the financial community in London.

"Management is obviously an important issue for the City (financial institutions) and if you can't have continuity then a man with a proven track record like Dalglish is the next best thing," said Nick Knight, who has researched soccer club finances for brokerage Nomura.
"The people of Newcastle may not think so but this may turn out to be a blessing in disguise."

Keegan stunned the soccer world and threw flotation plans into confusion last week when he walked out on the north-east club, saying he felt he had taken them as far as he could in his five years at the helm.

Dalglish has already tasted title success as a manager with Liverpool and Blackburn. No manager has ever won the English championship with three different clubs but few would bet against Scotsman Dalglish doing just that.

His Newcastle team is expected to be less spectacular than the one Keegan built but the hope is that he will rectify the glaring defensive weaknesses which undermined the goalscoring feats of England duo Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand.
Newcastle are still in contention for the league title and the F.A. and UEFA Cups this season.
They are the latest in a long line of British soccer clubs seeking to raise new funds and broaden ownership by joining the stock market.

The game is booming, with satellite broadcaster BSkyB pumping huge sums of money into the English premier league and fans flocking through the turnstiles at modernised stadiums as hooliganism declines.

English champions Manchester United are the model which clubs are seeking to emulate in the financial stakes. United's success on the pitch has been matched by growing profits off it and the club is now valued at over 400 million pounds.

Smaller premier league clubs such as Sunderland and Southampton, for whom survival in the top flight is the name of the game, have also seen their shares climb steeply in value since they joined the stock market recently.
Dealers believe there will be strong interest in the Newcastle listing.
"They will be the second-biggest quoted club in the market after Manchester United and I think they will do very well," said Alon Bull of Winterflood Securities. ($1=.5979 Pound)
